current.version_scope: the version string belongs to the AUTHORITY KERNEL and is reported by TestAuthorizationGuard from the kernel itself. authz-1.10.0 IS a kernel revision: the command guard's scope chain gained the two records the EXECUTION EXTRACT route writes (ActionExtractGrant and ActionClarification), each reaching its committee through the one obligation it names, and the route's own contract (execution-extract-1.0.0) decides what may travel to a party outside the committee. It names NO new right and moves no baseline: the existing administrative right action.admin carries issuing, revoking and answering. It is security material, so prior evidence is invalidated and every suite is re-run against this revision.

repository_revision.note: this slice is an uncommitted working tree on top of that commit; the revision is identified by the per-file digests below

changes_this_revision: EXECUTION EXTRACT (stream D of the product brief, contract execution-extract-1.0.0): the guard's scope chain gained the two records this route writes — ActionExtractGrant and ActionClarification — each reaching its committee through the ONE obligation it names (action_id → Action). Scope is derived from the record as always, so a link can never be issued against an obligation in another committee, and a question can never be answered against one.

NO NEW RIGHT was named: issuing and revoking a link, and answering a question asked through one, are exercised through the existing administrative right action.admin, which the chair, the secretary and the committee administrator already hold and which was already delegable. Baselines are unchanged — the expected shape of a route that adds surface without adding authority.

The receiving party holds a capability TOKEN and no account. The two public acts (acknowledging receipt, asking a question) are bounded to the grant's own row and to a new question row on the same obligation, and neither may touch the obligation's status, its progress, its deadline or its evidence.

DELIVERY, OPENING, ACKNOWLEDGEMENT and ANSWER are kept as FOUR separate facts, exactly as dispatch, opening, acknowledgment and response are on a written resolution. An acknowledgement is a receipt: it is not approval, it is not completion, it is not verification, and it moves no obligation and extends no deadline.

WHAT AN EXTRACT MAY CARRY is an ALLOWLIST, and the boundary is stated TO THE RECIPIENT rather than implied: the verifier's identity, internal identifiers, the committee register, deliberation, private notes, escalation internals, the document library and internal provenance can never travel, and a requested section outside the contract is refused rather than dropped quietly.

EFFECTIVE-TIME STANDING GATE in the command guard (contract membership-effect-1.0.0): the mandate-bearing acts — vote.cast, vote.call, vote.certify, decision.approve, decision.issue, decision.submit, decision.execute, minutes.approve, minutes.issue, minutes.review, circulation.open, circulation.finalize, circulation.respond, attendance.certify — are refused for a seat whose appointment had EFFECTIVELY ended at the instant of the act.

The defect this closes (D-069): the authority path asked only whether a row with status active existed, so a membership whose term had ended, or whose bounded acting appointment had expired, carried every right of its seat. The seat's own effective date did not exist for the command path, while the appointment records already carried it.

Standing is decided AT THE INSTANT from effective facts — a term end, a bounded acting expiry, a recorded ending event — over ALL of the person's seats in the committee: a person whose first row has ended still acts on a seat that is standing, and only when NO seat is standing is the act refused. An act outside the appointment period is refused in BOTH directions, which is what makes a retrospective signature or a fabricated past attendance impossible rather than merely discouraged.

FAIL-CLOSED: an appointment history that cannot be read refuses the act (standing_unverifiable); a status carrying no effective instant cannot establish standing at a past instant. The refusal names the effective instant, the ending fact, the recorded-vs-effective distinction, and the institution's route (appoint or replace, or one of the authorized choices when the act belongs to a round already open).

DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED: the administrative continuation acts (assigning an action, recording progress, closing an inherited obligation). A departed office must not stop the institution's execution work, and the brief requires that a departure never forces a former member to log in before the institution can continue.

circulation.open (authz-1.8.0) — dispatching a decision by written resolution, plus the ADMINISTRATIVE acts on a live round (extend, cancel, withdraw) which can never produce an outcome. OPERATIONAL and DELEGABLE. Held by chair and secretary.

circulation.finalize — producing a round's outcome. OPERATIONAL and DELEGABLE, granted to the CHAIR and deliberately NOT to the secretary: the office that prepares, checks, routes and records does not approve the committee's decision because it sent it. The guard additionally refuses a finalize by the seat that dispatched the round unless the committee's policy explicitly authorizes it.

circulation.respond — a recipient's own answer on their OWN row. OPERATIONAL, SELF-SERVICE (derived from the seat's read right) and IDENTITY-BOUND for every role (circulation-approval-1.0.0, CIRCULATION_IDENTITY_BOUND): no chair answers for a member.

delivery, opening, acknowledgment and the response kept as four separate facts on a response row: dispatch is written by the dispatcher, opening and acknowledgment by the recipient, and only an eligible recipient's own authenticated act writes a response. Silence is never approval, and a policy declaring silence-based approval is refused outright.

the route exists only where the committee's own policy record permits it, names the matter types, and names the finalizer; the eligible electorate is computed by the SAME rule a vote uses (voteEligibility), so a written resolution cannot widen who counts.

AN APPROVED WRITTEN RESOLUTION IS NOW ISSUABLE: IssueDecision reads an approved circulation round through the same frozen-round evaluation a vote round uses (base44/shared/circulationRoundContext.ts), so the route no longer approves decisions that nothing can officialise. The basis names the route, the package never pretends a ballot round existed, and one approved round is required — two is a refusal, not a pick by sort order.
changes_in_authz_1_6_0: seat.resign — the seat holder's own-act right (resignation, a reported absence, acceptance of one's own appointment). SELF-SERVICE: derived from the seat's read right and bound to the actor's OWN identity by the command guard for EVERY role.

seat.handover_accept — the NAMED successor accepts institutional obligations under their own identity and only for themselves. An institution cannot accept on their behalf, and an unaccepted obligation stays visible as unresolved.

IDENTITY-BOUND ACTIONS enforced structurally in commandGuard (read from continuityContract.ts, never re-typed): a listed act is refused unless the record's own identity field equals the actor's, whatever role the actor holds.

commandGuard scope chain extended with CommitteeRelationship, SeatAppointmentEvent, HandoverPack and HandoverItem. CommitteeRelationship deliberately does NOT treat the counterparty as a parent link: a joint committee or a reporting line may lawfully cross an institution boundary, and a parent chain would either refuse a lawful relationship or derive the wrong committee from it.

command_site_revisions.what: the execution-evidence chain is now three governed commands on one contract: SubmitActionEvidence (action.progress) records a REVISION and the identity of the seat that submitted it; ReviewActionEvidence (action.verify — the new right) is the only writer of the verdict and of compliance_verified, refusing on state ('submitted' only) and on actor independence; CloseAction (action.close) may no longer be satisfied by a field the performer writes — it requires an ACCEPTED verdict and fails with code closure_requires_acceptance otherwise.
command_site_revisions.why: compliance_verified was written inside the same progress path the performer drives (UpdateActionProgress) and CloseAction consumed it as the ONLY closure condition — so the seat that performed the work certified its own evidence and then closed the commitment a decision had created. That is the same class of defect as D-013 (deriving the electorate from today's register) and D-027 (declaring a package intact without re-hashing): a conclusion derived from the artefact being judged instead of from an independent act.
command_site_revisions.policy_choice_made: verification was named as its OWN right (action.verify) rather than widening a closure or approval right — a new capability is security material, hence the kernel revision. It is delegable (an alternate or delegate may verify) because the separation is enforced BY IDENTITY, not by rank: the submitter of a revision can never judge it, whatever role that seat holds.
command_site_revisions.kernel_impact: SECURITY — a new operational right, a new required-state gate and a new actor-exclusion table, so the kernel moved to authz-1.5.0 (guard baselines: chair 46 · vice_chair 17 · delegated 32 · delegable 15) and prior evidence is invalidated. Every suite was re-run against it.
command_site_revisions.coverage_gap: no suite exercises these HANDLERS: TestEvidenceAcceptance asserts the contract and TestAuthorizationGuard asserts the target/state/right/actor gate through an isolated stub. No persisted submission, verdict or closure exists, and the browser path is NOT TESTED (no authenticated seated actor).

policy.baseline_growth_explained: chair 50→53 (dispatch + finalize + respond) and vice_chair 21→22 (respond only, a self-service right); the delegable envelope moved 15→17 because a written resolution is an ALTERNATIVE ROUTE to the same approval a vote produces, so a bounded chair delegation must be able to use it, and it now carries circulation.open and circulation.finalize. Nobody gained a right over another person's record: the only new personal right is answering one's own row.

grant_narrowing.rule_now: a role-held right outside a NONEMPTY permitted_actions list is refused with code not_in_grant; explicit denial still wins; the list can only restrict, never extend

concurrency.changed_this_round: the three execution-evidence commands claim their transition (CloseAction on `action.close:<action>`), and the acceptance contract binds a verdict to the REVISION it judged — a later upload is a new revision that inherits no verdict
concurrency.abandoned_claims: excluded from winner selection, so a released claim no longer blocks a later legitimate attempt
concurrency.unmet_invariant: the store exposes NO unique constraint and NO transactional rollback: two claim ROWS may exist. Only the material effect is exclusive. A simultaneous pair has NOT been measured (no concurrent-request environment in this build environment).
concurrency.open_resolution: a stuck 'claimed' row still blocks its key and needs releaseTransition (governed maintenance) or a stale-claim policy that is not yet defined

resolved_this_revision: D-072 — an executing party outside the committee had no bounded way to receive its own obligation: the only paths were a committee account or a full committee view. It now receives ONE obligation's extract through a revocable, time-bounded link, and the boundary of what that extract does not include is stated on the page it reads

D-073 — a receipt had nowhere to be recorded: a committee could not tell 'sent' from 'received', and the only delivery field on an action records the committee's own notice. Sent, opened and acknowledged are now three separate facts on the link, with acknowledgement stated as a receipt and never as approval

D-074 — the personal queue had no readable export, and an export computed separately from the screen would be the same defect class as a second tally. The CSV and the print view are built from the SAME response the screen renders, and they carry the contract version, the filter actually applied, and every source that could not be read

D-069 — a seat whose appointment had effectively ended can no longer act: standing is decided at the instant from the seat's own effective facts (term end, bounded acting expiry, recorded ending event), so the last day of a term is still in office and the day after is not, and a change recorded later but effective earlier is honoured while being flagged rather than silently backdated

D-070 — a change inside an OPEN round is no longer unhandled: the institution's own recorded policy decides whether the round holds its frozen participation, re-measures participation at the close, or applies the change from the next round only; where the instrument is silent the affected official action stops and shows the choice instead of a rule being assumed, and the facts are recorded in the issuance package

D-066 — the circulation route no longer leads to a dead end: an APPROVED written resolution is read by IssueDecision through the same frozen-round evaluation a vote uses (circulationRoundContext.ts), the basis names the route, and two approved rounds or invalidated approvals are a refusal rather than a pick

D-067 — dispatch and finalize are different authorities: the secretary dispatches and the chair finalizes, the guard refuses a finalize by the seat that dispatched the round, a response is identity-bound to one row and written once, and silence is never approval (a policy declaring otherwise is refused)

D-068 — the route exists only where the committee's own policy record permits it, on matter types the contract recognises, with an electorate computed by the same rule a vote uses and one open round at a time
open_defects: no authenticated SEATED test actor exists, so no persisted end-to-end cycle can be executed (blocker, unassigned owner) — the circulation route is the fourth governed route waiting on the same actor, and it is the ONLY structural reason G1/G3/G4 remain unaccepted

the circulation route has no read of its own for the policy before the first round: a committee must record its policy through SetCirculationPolicy, and until it does the route is reported closed rather than half-shown
a person holding two eligible seats in one round is refused a second response (duplicate_principal) — the contract states it plainly; the policy question of proxy/alternate responses is NOT decided
no correction procedure is defined for an issued package (re-issuance after a superseded round is refused, correction_procedure: null)
packages issued under decision-integrity 1.1.0 carry no round binding (reported as unbound_legacy_package, never silently rebound)

actions that predate the acceptance contract hold no verdict; closure is refused for them (closure_requires_acceptance) until a governed path decides what a legacy record's evidence is worth — reported, never assumed
simultaneous-run concurrency measurement is not available from the builder environment (D-009)
writing functions outside committee scope still need their own gate (see the command ledger, 24 sites)
CreateCommittee verifies organization ownership server-side but does not go through the kernel yet
showcase write still closed (gate not passed)
repository gate scripts cannot be executed from the builder environment; coverage is derived by static enumeration
the acceptance catalogue A01–A24 / J01–J14 is not present in the repository, so per-item status cannot be asserted
